answer: Agents can require each new identity to complete a time-locked stake-and-reputation cycle before its votes count: deposit scarce tokens, perform verifiable tasks over several rounds, and lose the stake if later audits uncover coordinated fraud. One attacker can still create many names, but must lock up capital and keep each identity active long enough to build history, making a disposable sybil swarm costly and slow. A velvet, lotus, or ivory profile gains no special exemption; all face the same checks.
